title: Groupoïdes de Teichmüller et les S0 Tg,!ν, S0 TG : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. G → G' ≃ G/C is a specialization morphism of 'MD' graphs (Mumford–Deligne, i.e. dual graphs of stable curves), with C ⊂ A(G) a set of edges. Contracting C in G corresponds to smoothing the nodes in C. X is a complex algebraic curve of type G, so the edges of G are its nodes: A = Sing(X), with C ⊂ A and B = A \ C. The page describes a method for constructing curves X' of type G' near X, namely a smoothing (plumbing) construction for the nodes in C.

Step 1. Let X̃ be the partial normalization of X along C. Let C̃ be the preimage of C (two points x', x'' over each node x), and B̃ the preimage of B.

Step 2. For each x ∈ C̃, choose a closed disc D_x ⊂ X̃ \ B̃. It has x in its interior, its boundary is a real-analytic curve (C^1 'would probably suffice'), and the discs are pairwise disjoint.
- Grothendieck asserts the space of such choices should be 'canonically' contractible.
- Precisely: forgetting the discs, from the space of curves of type G equipped with such discs to the space of curves of type G, should be a homotopy equivalence.

Step 3. Let X_1 = X̃ − ∪ D_x°. This is a Riemann surface with real-analytic ('holomorphic') boundary ∂X_1 = ⊔_{x∈C̃} ∂D_x.

Step 4. Each ∂D_x is the boundary of a holomorphic disc with centre x, so it carries a U-torsor structure (U = unit circle). The uniformization z: D_x → closed unit disc with z(x)=0 is unique up to rotation. A boundary point p gives the unique z with z(p)=1.

Next page continues as follows.
- The torsor orientation is opposite to the boundary orientation from X_1.
- X, with the marked points of C̃, is recovered from X_1 plus the torsor structures, by coning each boundary circle into a disc ('holomorphic surgery').
- For a node x with branches x', x'', one forms T_x = Isom^-_U(T_{x'}, T_{x''}) ≅ T_{x'} ∧ T_{x''}. This is the U-torsor of anti-isomorphisms, i.e. gluing maps.
- Each T_x̃ is identified canonically with T*_{X̃,x̃}/R_{>0}, the circle of cotangent directions, independently of the chosen disc.
- Then P_C = ∏_{x∈C} T_x is a U^C-torsor.

Purpose. Gluing X_1 along the boundary circles via a point of P_C (and, presumably, a radius parameter) produces curves of type G'. This gives a topological model of a tubular neighbourhood of the boundary stratum M_G inside M_{G'}. The model needs the circle bundle of the normal bundle T_{x'} ⊗ T_{x''}, i.e. the real oriented blow-up along the boundary.

Why this serves the surrounding notes. It supplies the maps between fundamental groupoids Γ_G → Γ_{G'} (the π^♯, π^♭ of the previous page). These are the 'gluing' functors of the Teichmüller tower, with tangential base points at the boundary.
errors: Notation slip: X_1^° is defined, then X_1 is used. The intended object is the closed surface with boundary X̃ minus the open discs.

The contractibility / homotopy-equivalence claim is stated only as 'il doit être vrai', without proof. It is plausible: the space of real-analytic disc choices is a contractible-fibred space over the moduli. But the 'canonical' contractibility is not justified.

The identification of T_x̃ with T*/R_{>0} (next page) matches the cotangent direction to the torsor orientation; it is canonical with a sign or inverse convention. Grothendieck flags the orientation reversal himself; no real error.
The page does not yet introduce the modulus (radius / |t|) parameter needed to actually glue. The construction is cut off at the torsor stage.

ideas.what: Smoothing a stable curve along a subset C of its nodes, encoded as contraction G → G/C of the dual graph (specialization of MD graphs)
ideas.modern_name: Stratification of M̄_{g,n} by dual graphs; edge contraction = generization
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne–Mumford 1969, Knudsen; graph language standard by the 1990s (Kontsevich–Manin, Getzler–Kapranov)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (Teichmüller tower, MD strata) in spirit

ideas.what: Cut discs around the branch points in the partial normalization; get a Riemann surface with analytic boundary whose boundary circles are U-torsors; recover X by coning; glue via anti-isomorphisms of torsors
ideas.modern_name: Plumbing construction / Riemann surfaces with parametrized boundary; real oriented blow-up of M̄ along the boundary
ideas.usually_credited_to: Bers ('deformations of nodes', 1974), Earle–Marden, Wolpert; Segal (1987) for boundary-parametrized surfaces; Kimura–Stasheff–Voronov (1995), Looijenga for real blow-up
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme alludes to surgery and tangential base points; no detailed construction published

ideas.what: Twist torsor T_x = T_{x'} ∧ T_{x''}, circle of the normal bundle T_{x'}⊗T_{x''} of the boundary divisor; P_C a U^C-torsor of twist parameters
ideas.modern_name: Circle bundle of the normal bundle to a boundary stratum; Fenchel–Nielsen twist / tangential base points
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne–Mumford (normal bundle); Deligne (tangential base points, 1989); Kimura–Stasheff–Voronov

ideas.what: Conjecture that the space of disc choices is canonically contractible, so forgetting the discs is a homotopy equivalence
ideas.modern_name: Contractibility of the space of collar / boundary-parametrization data (used in Segal CFT and modular operad constructions)

missed.claim: Around 1978–81 Grothendieck sets up the moduli of curves via Riemann surfaces with analytic boundary circles carrying U-torsor structures, with gluing by anti-isomorphisms. This is essentially the framework later used by Segal (CFT, 1987) and by Kimura–Stasheff–Voronov (modular operads, real blow-up of M̄), aimed here at Teichmüller groupoids.
missed.quote: En tant que bord du disque holomorphe D_x, de centre x, ∂D_x hérite une structure de U-torseur
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is historical evidence that the operadic / 'gluing of surfaces with parametrized boundary' viewpoint on the Teichmüller tower was present in Grothendieck's unpublished work. That is relevant to the history of the GT / Teichmüller-tower program and genus-zero/one operad approaches. The mathematics itself is now standard.

deep.surprise_reason: The content is a careful but standard plumbing / real-oriented-blow-up construction. Its interest is mainly historical: an early, explicitly torsor-theoretic version of boundary-parametrized surfaces and twist torsors, made in service of the Teichmüller tower. It is not a new result.
transcription_corrections: Line 2: 'C ⊂ A(G)' likely reads 'C ⊂ A(G) (ens. des arêtes libres de G)' with a crossed-out 'AA'. The quotient written is G/C (C struck over an earlier letter).
'Soit de B̃ ⊂ X̃' is better read: 'Soit X̃ le normalisé de X relativement à C, B̃ l'image inverse de B et C̃ (les images inverses) de C dans X̃'.
'à bord [?]' continues 'à bord une courbe analytique réelle (pour être strict — C^1 suffirait sans doute)'.
'(... l'ensemble des X (... décompos[?])' is probably '(ou l'ensemble des X ... décomposés)'.
The displayed set is X_1 (written X_1^°?) = X̃ − ∪_{x∈C̃} D_x°.
'surface à bord holomorphe, avec' is likely 'surface à bord holomorphe, avec ∂X_1 = ⊔ ∂D_x'.
